findings.explanation: The second validation block on var.members rejects only the literal strings allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers. A member value of the form domain:example.com is not caught by this check or by HLD_GCP_024 (which uses the same not_one_of [allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers] condition), yet it grants read access to every user in that Google Workspace (or consumer Gmail) domain — a blast radius that scales with the domain's user count and is easy to introduce by mistake (e.g. a `user:` grant missing its prefix, or copy-pasting a domain-wide grant from another module). Neither the deterministic engine nor this module's own defense-in-depth validation can catch it because it's a graph-independent, single-attribute string check with no enumerable 'safe' set — a domain: grant is sometimes intentional (internal company-wide registries) and sometimes a mistake, which is why this needs a human decision rather than an auto-fix.
findings.remediation: Decide whether domain: principals should be allowed for this module. If not, extend the validation condition to also reject them, e.g. add `&& !anytrue([for m in var.members : startswith(m, "domain:")])`. If domain-wide grants are intentionally supported, document that in the variable description so it's clear the omission is deliberate.
findings.suppression_reason: User decision (2026-08-12): validation hardening of variables.tf is not the focus of this module. Left as-is; HLD_GCP_515 (now shipped) still flags domain: grants for any consumer at scan time.
findings.title: members validation blocks the two public sentinels but not domain-wide grants

suggested_policies.rationale: coverage_by_type[google_artifact_registry_repository_iam_member] has 3 entries (HLD_GCP_024, HLD_GCP_210, HLD_GCP_450) and none of them inspect the member attribute for a domain: prefix — HLD_GCP_024 only rejects the two universal sentinels (allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers). A domain: grant is a distinct, unambiguous, structurally-detectable pattern (a string prefix match on member) that's broadly applicable to any Terraform using this resource type, not just this repo. Severity is kept LOW/advisory rather than a hard fail because domain-wide grants are a legitimate choice for some internal registries — this is a review flag, not a ban.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_515
name: Artifact Registry IAM bindings granting domain-wide access should be reviewed
principle: identity-and-access
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  A `domain:` principal in an Artifact Registry IAM member grants repository
  access to every user of an entire Google Workspace (or consumer Gmail)
  domain. Unlike a scoped user/group/service-account grant, the blast radius
  scales with the domain's user count and is easy to add by mistake (e.g. a
  `user:` grant missing its prefix). holden's existing HLD_GCP_024 only
  rejects the two universal sentinel principals (allUsers,
  allAuthenticatedUsers) and does not flag domain: grants, which can be
  nearly as broad depending on the domain.
remediation: |
  Confirm the domain-wide grant is intentional. If narrower access is
  sufficient, replace it with specific user:, group:, or serviceAccount:
  principals:

    resource "google_artifact_registry_repository_iam_member" "readers" {
      member = "group:artifact-readers@example.com"
      # ...
    }
resources:
  google_artifact_registry_repository_iam_member:
    path: member
    not_matches: "^domain:"
